description:
We are Team TerraPulse for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are developing "Stay & Build Egypt", a platform utilizing NASA Earth data to map environmental and healthcare pressures in Egypt, guiding medical professionals to areas where they can create maximum impact.

Looking For: Web developers (HTML/CSS/JS/React), data analysts (Python/Pandas), and UI/UX designers
summary:
TerraMed Pulse: Stay & Build Egypt transforms 31 years of NASA Earth observation data (1995–2025) into actionable insights to address two interconnected challenges in Egypt: increasing environmental stress and physician migration.

While climate change creates different health challenges across Egyptian governorates, the continuous emigration of medical professionals leaves many communities with limited access to essential healthcare services.

Our platform bridges Earth science and healthcare through an interactive system that analyzes data from NASA POWER, MERRA-2, MODIS, and GLDAS to detect environmental trends and identify regional vulnerabilities. Using the Health Need Index (HNI), TerraMED Pulse connects environmental pressures with healthcare needs and provides an "I Am a Doctor" Impact Matcher to guide physicians toward underserved governorates where their specialties are most needed.

Additionally, our Physician Observatory collects doctors' feedback, while the What-If Policy Lab simulates potential solutions such as financial incentives, mobile clinics, and urban greening.

Our mission is to encourage physicians to stay and build Egypt by transforming NASA data into meaningful opportunities for healthcare improvement.
details:
TerraMed Pulse is an interactive decision-support platform that bridges environmental science and healthcare planning. Rather than claiming climate data directly solves Egypt’s physician emigration crisis, our project uses 31 years of NASA Earth observations (1995-2025) to provide critical context: mapping exactly where environmental stressors are multiplying local healthcare burdens. By visualizing this climate stress alongside workforce metrics, we create a "clinical impact compass" that highlights where a doctor's presence is most urgently needed.

To build this solution, we utilized a robust and modern tech stack. Data extraction was powered by direct NASA APIs to pull extreme heat and aerosol variables from NASA POWER (MERRA-2), vegetation and land surface temperatures from MODIS, and soil moisture from GLDAS-2.1 Noah. We utilized Python to process these massive datasets and conduct rigorous Mann-Kendall trend testing, ensuring we only highlight statistically significant climate shifts. We then overlaid these stressors with demographic grids from NASA SEDAC and healthcare metrics from WHO and CAPMAS data.

To make these complex insights accessible and responsive, the frontend was built using React.js and styled with Tailwind CSS, creating a fast, modular, and user-friendly interface. Within this React ecosystem, we integrated Leaflet.js to render interactive spatial maps for our "Earth System Trend Detective," and Chart.js to power dynamic, real-time data visualizations.

The project's creativity lies in its translation layer and dual-audience design. For doctors, the "Doctor Impact Matcher" uses the Leaflet.js maps to correlate medical specialties with local environmental drivers, guiding them to underserved regions like Aswan. Simultaneously, the Chart.js-powered "What-If Policy Lab" provides decision-makers with a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) simulator. While NASA data defines the map of environmental vulnerability, this simulator allows leaders to test evidence-based retention levers against real emigration drivers. Ultimately, TerraMed Pulse uses Earth observations to illuminate clinical need, providing the contextual evidence required to help doctors "Stay & Build Egypt."
